claim: SHA-pinned original DLL-001 SkillDataMan.ParseRSFData MethodDef 0x0600525F (1735 IL bytes, SHA 09000cc6b6e149540eb76d0865d8dd3aadcab1cd6bf8493286db768377c18cae) has exact 189-byte IL window 0x017F..0x023B (SHA a5a334f393cc1a57fb99052c3dc9d5c980fad164a7cd51741c5f7b511f41a7fb). It loads three successive unsigned source bytes from parser arg2+26, +27 and +28 using the original postincrement cursor semantics. From byte+26, original IL stores (byte & 0xF0)>>4 in original SkillData.atkPrmType_Main and (byte&0x0F) in SkillData.atkPrmType_Sub. From byte+27 it stores the corresponding high and low nibbles in SkillData.defPrmType_Main and defPrmType_Sub. It then tests source byte+28 bits 0,1,2,3 independently; for each nonzero bit it ORs original SkillData.flags with respectively 0x0200, 0x0400, 0x0800, 0x1000. Every zero-bit branch skips only its corresponding OR and resumes at the next bit check or subsequent parser instructions. All field names, metadata row bytes, source opcodes and four targets are observed in the original DLL; field labels do not establish actual gameplay effects.
